notes.title: June Dev Update!
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

Over the past month, we’ve been focused on improving the core combat experience in The Signal, especially around how it feels to move and shoot in first-person.


Why We're Making Changes
The Signal is a narrative-driven game set on an alien planet. Our original vision leaned heavily into puzzle-solving to supplement the environmental storytelling and to support the unfolding mystery of the world. However, after multiple playtests, we realized that the slower gameplay rhythm was detracting from the overall experience, and pulling focus away from the story.

The feedback was clear: a snappier, more reactive moment-to-moment experience would better support player immersion and pacing.


What We've Changed
To support this shift, we’ve made major updates:

Redesigned the animation system to support a more responsive feel.

Moved to a more data-driven system for scalability and easier iteration.

Reworked enemy AI to add more variety and personality to encounters.

Improved terrain navigation and shooting feel to make first-person gameplay more satisfying.

All of this ties into our renewed focus on making each encounter more dynamic and meaningful.

[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcjQ9E68F_XwUiif6wHIwNxFSOSOQQaebfybstcHrUtPkdzWNSNOPxXfblE5AJySi0PsThBAZb6t2NrwvIF1JD2LEoLuSor5xoAh-uSeIoLE1i85JZY0Q1Y5z2QPvUdRjYtDLxWWA?key=yBOXaZAnxuSWu26EzT7k0A"]


World Structure Rework
Throughout our playtests, we also tried several different world structures. The version that resonated most with playtesters—and our team—is one that centers around a single hub area. You’ll build your base here and head out on expeditions from this central location. This setup not only fits our gameplay better, it also aligns more closely with our story direction.
With the world structure design locked in, we finally started working on level design that we intend to carry into the final game. We can’t wait to test this out with players. 



[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcux6GgTEY3FpKQtWhSfcA0jIeQEllCmaIGmzLg8YPrDI-HQDMMq8SLWt8DPP2QYjyTDw9dDcDgMiHAjklNoSh_MI38UmgFATrwG9pZtZqgt4iH7EPPwgxuq_VhY2rwjuP2kkOy?key=yBOXaZAnxuSWu26EzT7k0A"]
What’s Next?
We're continuing to polish combat and improve overall aesthetics. Our goal is to put together a playable slice that brings everything together for another round of playtesting.

If you’d like to take part, head over to our Steam page and click the green Playtest button to sign up:
 

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1830110/THE_SIGNAL/"][/dynamiclink]
Thanks for the Feedback
Your feedback has been essential in guiding our decisions. Testing early and often helps us stay grounded and avoid tunnel vision. We’re excited to share more soon.

If you’d like to stay updated, follow us on social media:

Twitter: @TheSignalGame

Bluesky: thesignalgame.bsky.social

TikTok: @TheSignalGame



— The Signal Dev Team

notes.title: We're Revamping our Vehicles!
notes.content:
Hello explorers,

It’s been a while since our last proper update—a long while, in fact! We’ve been laser focused on our work behind the scenes, and today we’d like to share what we’ve been up to!

🧭 The Road So Far

We kicked off the year by reviewing all the feedback from our Winter Holiday playtest. Your insights helped shape our design direction, and we’ve been iterating on both your feedback and our internal vision for the game.

The first few months were about laying a new foundation. We expanded the team with new members and interns, which allowed us to form focused strike teams: Combat, Build/Craft, UI, and Level Design. This new structure is helping us move faster and more intentionally.
But scaling up wasn’t just about adding people—it was about cleaning up. We removed all placeholders, transitioning away from using any store-bought prototyping assets, and doubled down on reinforcing our art direction. Every asset now reflects our style and should run efficiently on a wide range of machines.

⚙️ Under the Hood: Unreal Engine 5.5 & System Refactors

We also dove into code refactors and upgraded to Unreal Engine 5.5 the very day it dropped. Among the biggest technical changes was integrating the Gameplay Ability System, which will make our combat and action systems far easier to iterate on. To do this, we had to go in and modify ALL of our existing features, so it was a lot of work! It will be worth it, though. 

🚗 Vehicles Are Back—and Better Than Ever

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44513777/b3525f5f9bed69ddf0813f676a81751a3d06d8b4.png
After the engine upgrade, we moved our focus to vehicles. If you remember our May 2024 playtest, you might recall the early version of our Custom Vehicle system. We ended up pulling it from the last two tests—not because we abandoned it, but because we wanted to integrate your feedback into the customization feature. Our customization flow had too many steps, and needed to be streamlined. 

We were looking into different technological approaches for our design, and with UE5.5’s release, the moment finally arrived.

Here’s what’s new:

Chaos Modular Vehicle Plugin: We moved from Chaos Vehicles to Chaos Modular Vehicles—an experimental but promising solution that has the added benefit of drastically improving physics stability. No more flipping out (literally). 


Garage Overhaul: We’ve shifted vehicle customization from the Workshop to a dedicated Garage, complete with a streamlined building flow. Parts now snap together more cleanly, creating more intuitive and rewarding vehicle crafting.


Improved Terrain Handling: Our new suspension system hugs terrain more precisely than ever, making driving across rugged alien landscapes feel smooth and responsive.


🚀 Why Vehicles Matter in The Signal

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44513777/fbca78e4e7ac3445e09fb609dd1289f2e7b45b0f.gif
Vehicles aren’t just a side feature—they’re central to your journey. You build them as part of your crafting loop, then use them during extraction runs to haul back valuable resources. They need to feel powerful, reliable, and worth the effort—and we’re committed to making sure they do.


🛠️ What’s Next?
We’re excited to let players try out the new vehicle system soon. But before that, we’re polishing up a few final pieces. Expect more concrete news in the weeks ahead.

In the meantime, we’d love to hear from you:

🗨️ What kind of vehicle customization would you like to see in The Signal? Let us know in the comments!

Thanks for being part of the journey. Don’t forget to wishlist us on Steam if you haven’t already—every wishlist helps us more than you know. And also, don't forget to follow us on our socials!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1830110/THE_SIGNAL/

Stay tuned,
The Signal Dev Team

notes.title: Playtest open during Winter Holidays!
notes.content:
Instead of closing our playtest last week, we are taking things one step further and opening it to a wider audience. Starting Thursday 19 December 2024 we'll be admitting 1,000 new players who have requested playtest access -- these people will receive emails that the playtest is open. 

But maybe you tried the playtest previously at some point? If you did then YOU TOO will have access to the playtest, you just won't receive an email. Steam is weird that way. The playtest will also be available to Discord community members who have access and/or who claim a key.

We are going to leave this playtest open until  Monday 6 January 2025. Hopefully follks will have some time to test out the new build over the holidays. 

This is our gift to you! And all we ask in return is for you to complete our FEEDBACK FORM!  Whether you played for 5 hours or rage quit afer 10 minutes -- we absolutely want to hear about your experience. It is extremely valuable feedback and truly will help us decide what to work on next.

This is an early Pre-Alpha build, and you may experience bugs, crashes, or performance issues. It's a work in progress but we feel like there's a good experience in there and we hope you will get something out of it. 

Please note that this build has a Save System, so you don't need to complete the playthrough in one sitting. Since we will most likely be changing many more things between now and the next playtest/demo, your save will NOT carry over beyond this playtest.  

Ways to play:

  Join our Discord and claim a key in the playtest-chat channel
  If you playtested before look for the green Join The Signal Playtesting "PLAY NOW" button on our Steam page.
  Keep an eye on your inbox for an invitation -- maybe you're one of the lucky 1,000 players!

And if you don't get access or can't find the time to play, we absolutely promise there will be another playtest in early 2025. We hope everyone has fun and gets through the holiday season -- we'll see eveyone next year. And as always, please do join the conversation either here on Steam or through Discord -- we love hearing from players!

P.S. We just joined BlueSky - https://bsky.app/profile/goosebyte.bsky.social

notes.title: Discord-Exclusive PreAlpha Playtest Weekend
notes.content:
We're launching a new Prealpha Playtest TOMORROW (Friday December 13, 2024) morning, at 10am EST. The plyatest will run until Tuesday morning, 10am EST. 

There's so much new stuff in here, I won't ruin the surprise by listing it in bullet point format. 
We've gone into uncharted territory on some of our design choices and have a few features that definitely require some more iteration on the tech side, so there may be some bugs, but we believe the experience should be smooth enough to gather some good feedback. 

There is also some content that's still in early stages, so some things are not fully realized, but we felt that including these would help flesh out our vision more, and give you a better sense of the direction we're heading in. 

The build DOES have a save feature, since the playtest is too long to fit into one session for some people. The save/load system should also help in case you encounter bugs, but save/load sometimes also introduces some additional minor bugs. We don't have a dedicated QA team, but we think we've covered most of the really bad ones. If you encounter bugs, please feel free to let us know about them in the 'submit-bug-report' section of the Playtesting Discord channel. 

This playtest is CLOSED and EXCLUSIVE to the Discord Community. If you like what you see, invite your friends to the Discord so they can take part in this journey, too! 

We do hope to eventually re-open the playtest to more players (ones that sign up via Steam), but that depends on the early feedback we get from people in here. 

We're super excited to see what you think of the build, and ask that everyone please hit the "feedback" button in the main menu and share their thoughts on this build. 

Hope you all have a wonderful weekend and enjoy our latest creation. 

- Theo

How to join this playtest:
- Click Here to join our Discord for The Signal
- Navigate to the 'playtest-chat' discussion and Grab a Key!
- Redeem your key when the playtest is open (Friday 13 Dec 10AM EST until Tuesday 17 Dec 10AM EST)
NOTE: If you've acessed our playtest before, you won't need a key -- the app will be open to returning playtesters without a key during the times listed above.

notes.title: Pre-Alpha Playtest Starts Now - Get Ready to Break Boundaries 🚀
notes.content:
Dear Explorers, 

We’re so pleased to announce the new playtest is ready to go and waiting for you to jump in. For the next 2 weeks we’ll be gathering feedback on our latest focus, capsules, as well as some other new mechanics and features across the game. We're still early in development and as such, we're so excited to have you, the community, on board for the journey helping guide the direction of THE SIGNAL through regular playtests, so don't be afraid to give feedback wherever you can - on Steam, Discord or elsewhere, as it all makes a huge difference. Read on for a look at some of the key additions as well as an overview of all of the new content being added! 

Capsules
Take your inventions on the go! Instantly deploy your stored inventions with a simple toss - equipment, structures and even vehicles can be carried with you on your expedition! Capsules are a super interesting concept for us, because we think they’ll bridge the gap between typically distinct game loops. We’re looking to blur the lines between traversal, combat, and crafting loops by tossing (pardon the pun!) these into the mix. 

Mouse & Keyboard Support
The number one piece of feedback we received after our first playtest was “Mouse & Keyboard!” – so our Design team spent some time on this and got a first playable version in! Let us know how it's working for you once you've had a chance to test it out. 

Localization
We swapped out all of our hard-coded text, so that we can support more languages! You can find the new options for this playtest on the Steam page and they include French, German, Spanish, Italian, Spanish, and more! We will be gradually adding more over the coming playtests. Currently the localization in-game is somewhat placeholder and we'd love to work with the community as we grow to ensure it's in as strong a place as possible as we progress through to launch! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44513777/a8d4103fcc096d181c0d7219f17794ffb7311818.png

Gameplay:

 Removed Oxygen - Don’t fret! Oxygen will come back when we have more time to fix it! 
 Precise Build Mode - Now only available when the player is within the Network. 
 New Vehicle Chassis & Options - Ditch the car, and take off on a bike instead! Wheel and Hover options are available
 Ping Scan - Explorers have a brand new system to help locate crucial resources and other points of interest. 
 New Points of Interest – our Art team suggested some cool new structures to explore, linked to the Dead Explorer objective. We’re not going to say more than that… you have to play to find out.
 Barrier Fragment - Dare we call it a “BEARIER”? If a bear or other creature tries to chomp your face off, we’re developing a sort of energy fence that can contain them long enough to let you scan or interact with them.


UI/UX & Graphics:

 UI/UX changes for the Multitool - We rearranged the multitool options and icons; This will continue to be iterated on as we add new features to the game.
 Reworked HUD - We moved the health bar and Network indicator to the top-left, and added Capsule inventory in the bottom right.
 Improved surface snapping in Workshop and Build Mode - Playtesters asked for this, so we delivered it! Hopefully way less annoying gaps between the things you build and where you want to place them on. 


General Changes:

 Draft Naming - Another huge request! Now you can name your drafts so you know what’s what. We haven’t set this up to work well with a controller yet, but it’s on our roadmap. 
 Improved vehicle handling/driving (they should flip less) - Some people might prefer when they flip more. Let us know what you think! 
 New Objective flow – Our last playtest really held your hand through a set of objectives. The intention was that we wanted to onboard the player as fast as possible to a complex and totally custom crafting workshop system. But as a playtest it also over-structured the first time user experience and limited what the player could mess around with. So now we’ve replaced most of that with a “discovery mission” – scan and learn about this biome, get to messing about whenever you want!
 Dead Explorer narrative mission – find out what happened to the previous expedition but be careful! Voiced by Jeremiah Costello who was casting director on Game of Thrones (video game) and has voiced characters in Dead Synchronicity, Pineview Drive and Husk.
 An easter egg from a different sci fi universe 👀 
 Toxic Gas is on longer linked to Alien Junk - Gases come from gas vents, and can be extracted with the right tool. Removing Alien junk still helps the ecofootprint score, but we have bigger plans for this for a later update. 
 Reminder: Invented drafts from past game sessions can be ‘uploaded’ and reused in a new session via a cheat. We don’t have a save system implemented yet, but this is a shortcut to get access to your inventions again if you experience a crash or interruption in your play session! 
 Added useful links in the Main Menu - you can now provide playtest feedback from there, and can also sign up for our newsletter to stay up-to-date on the latest developments. 
 Ecofootprint system modifications - Fewer player actions upset the ecosystem.
 Character run speed slowed down.
 Time of day speed slowed down.
 And of course various crash and bug fixes along the way.

[previewyoutube=Jf5yuG8Ma2A;full][/previewyoutube]

We can't wait to hear what you get up to out there, happy exploring!

notes.title: Pre-Alpha Playtest Notes and Limitations + FAQ
notes.content:
Hey Explorer!

Here is some information for you on the current playtest build (2024-04-12):

1. Progress is currently not saveable between sessions. Completing the playtest will bring you back to the main menu. If you spend 5 hours building a sky city then you will lose your creation!

2. Features/limitations to keep in mind:

- Creature Repellent: When a creature is in range while it is materialized, the creature won’t be repelled until it re-enters the range.
- Vehicle Physics: Past a certain number of fragments added to a vehicle (~20), expect it to be unstable (in other words: go flying).
- Currently, it’s on Gamepad/controller!

3. The playtest is currently singleplayer as we are early in our process.

4. Playtest is in English right now, plans for language support are in the works.

If you're interested in a more thorough FAQ, check out the pinned posts on our Steam Forum.

Happy gaming! We look forward to hearing your thoughts.

notes.title: The Signal Pre-Alpha Playtest Must-Knows
notes.content:
Hey Explorers!

Lots of news for you, so buckle up!

The playtest will be going live on Friday at 10:00 AM EST/7:00 PT. If you haven’t signed up for the playtest yet, well, whatcha waiting for!? Hop onto our Steam page and sign up using the playtest button. You’ll have until Tuesday 10AM EST/7:00 PT to play.

5. We’ll have more stuff coming your way soon. Our goal is always to be as transparent as possible with all of you, so we can’t wait to share what’s next!

Best,

Goose Byte

notes.title: Crafting in The Signal
notes.content:
So we’re making a crafting game? YUP! We asked Goose Byte game designer Alexandre “Breeze” Brisebois to break down some the “making of” a whole new crafting system from scratch:

“One of the challenges which has come up while working on our crafting system is the idea of crafting in context. Traditional crafting – where a player builds a thing inside the world – has a lot of natural feedback: when I’m building a house or an outpost I can see the area I’m building in and build around obstacles. If I need to build a bridge I know when I’ve hit the other side because I can see it. But by moving some of the crafting into an external space (i.e. into a Workshop) it can be easy to make mistakes in the details you would see naturally in the world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44513777/eda75016a10a96e585dfb1d025b61ea0fd183126.png
Our approach attempts to alleviate repetition in crafting by letting players create reusable drafts, but it’s natural (and desirable for a game) that every problem doesn’t have the exact same solution. Balancing crafting around eliminating repetition in the broad strokes and helping players focus on the details that need to be changed is a fun design challenge, both for the UX of the workshop and build modes, and how we're building the environment you’ll be exploring. 

We’ve been hard at work on UX improvements for the Workshop and Build modes lately and the work has been paying off. As we improved the UX we saw different members of the team not only produce different kinds of drafts, but watching them use the workshop… It's like seeing inside their thought process. 

Watching new members of the team try the crafting for the first time, or seeing what kind of habits the old hands have developed has been very affirming because it’s showcasing a lot of variety. Even in the early stages it’s clear that our crafting system lends itself to individual expression and I can’t wait to see what kinds of drafts players will share once they get their hands on the system.”

What do you think? Who did it better?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44513777/c834fb54ca01b57ead3e1758a376eb1ec92830f6.png
What are some of your favourite crafting systems in games? Join our Discord and let us know!
 - Goose Byte

notes.title: Starting our journey with the REVEAL TRAILER
notes.content:
One of the biggest challenges for any studio, solo devs or indie teams, is sharing your work to the public. It’s the most vulnerable part of any creative process, in fact. This is why we are so proud to finally bring you on the first step of this expedition, with a REVEAL TRAILER!

[previewyoutube=ptYyOCbhobc;full][/previewyoutube] 
Have you seen it yet? We really tried to cram a lot into this reveal – how do you put all those ideas into 100 seconds?

We know what we want to make, and we know how we intend to get there. It’s never a straight path. It weaves through dark forests and dangerous swampland (maybe mirroring our in-game progression?). It’s as triumphant as making it to the peak of a tall mountain, and as devastating as accidentally dropping your phone into a bottomless pit. The path isn’t safe or obvious. There are a lot of smaller problems to face along the way.

Like the expression says: the journey is its own reward. While we are far from the end of that journey, it feels great to be here, starting our ascent. We have all our gear and supplies and have finally made it to the first base camp, ever eager to take that next step.

Anyway, we’re making a game that we want to play. So far, it’s satisfying, intriguing and fun and we’ve only just gotten started. We’ll make it to the top, and we’re hoping you’ll join us along the way.

- Goose Byte
